drafts.draft_en:
You're 30 with $100k saved. Pick ONE:

• Buy a Philly rowhome at 65% of after-repair value and rent it
• Put it all in an index fund
• Keep it in cash and wait for a crash

No "split it." One choice. Why?
drafts.pattern: Pick-ONE fork, same shape as Shagun's 48.9k post (three concrete options, one choice). Grounded in Bar's 65% all-in rule. Asks for opinions, promises no returns.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head, 10s. Three fingers up, one per option, with each option on screen. End on 'One choice. Why?' and point at the camera.

drafts.draft_en:
A lot of owners who borrowed cheap have loans coming due.

Some can't refinance at today's rates. Some just want out.

That's where the deals are. Not on Zillow. With a seller who has a deadline.

If you could ask that owner one question, what would it be?
drafts.pattern: Rides Cardone's 'wall of maturing debt' / 'when the banks call' angle (7.6k today, RE + BTC run at 33.8k–48.6k) but keeps it to wholesaling deal flow. Question close for replies.
drafts.video_tip: Walk-and-talk, 15s, on a Philly block. Point at a rowhome, say the 'seller with a deadline' line, then put the closing question on screen.

drafts.draft_en:
Got a raise?

The first thing it buys decides if it was really a raise.

A $600/month car upgrade is $7,200 a year. That's a down payment you traded for a nicer commute.

What's the biggest raise trap you've seen?

drafts.video_tip: Screen record, 12s. Type '$600 x 12 = $7,200' in your notes app, then type 'down payment' under it and cross out 'nicer commute'. Read the question as the last beat.
